title: Widow-First Retention Drills for Wealth Advisors
one_liner: Sell independent advisors an annual 'if one of us dies' rehearsal for couples, because the defection risk sits at the first spouse's death, not with the kids.
customer: Independent RIAs and small wealth teams ($150M-$2B AUM) whose median client is 65+. The buyer is the firm principal or COO.
problem: The industry spends on next-gen events with heirs. Cerulli says about $54T of the transfer is spousal and about $40T of that goes to widowed women. The survivor is grieving, holds a house full of logins and unknown accounts, and has to decide whether to keep the advisor. Advisors are commonly said to lose most widows within a year (widely cited, verify). The cause is usually friction, not performance.
solution: A 90-minute 'Survivor Fire Drill' run by the advisor's team with a software kit. Each spouse's death is simulated in turn. The tool builds a First-90-Days playbook: who to call, which accounts exist, which autopays must keep running, and where the documents are. It audits titling and beneficiaries from the survivor's point of view and flags single points of failure, such as only one spouse knowing the passwords. It then schedules pre-agreed advisor check-ins at day 3, 14, 45 and 90. The advisor gets a dashboard of which couples have done the drill and where their exposure is.
why_now: Cerulli's Sept 2026 work frames retention of the transfer as the priority, and 89% of surveyed firms call family meetings essential. Wealth managers are buying heir-engagement tools, yet the first wave of money is spousal and the widow is under-served. Cheap document ingestion and secure vaults make the kit affordable for small firms.
revenue_model: $300-$700 per household per year billed to the firm, or a $25-40K/yr platform fee for a 100-household book. The ROI pitch: keeping one $1.5M widow at a 1% fee is worth $15K a year.
non_obvious_insight: The heir-retention narrative aims at the wrong person on the wrong day. Widows rarely leave over portfolio returns. They leave because nobody made the first 90 days easy. A rehearsal also works where estate planning fails, because people avoid 'planning' but will attend a scheduled drill.
first_30_days: Recruit 3-5 RIAs through advisor communities and podcasts. Run drills by hand with a spreadsheet and printed binder for each firm's 10 oldest couples. Record time-to-locate-accounts and the number of single-point-of-failure findings. Charge a $2.5K pilot fee and turn the findings into a retention case study the advisor can show prospects.

title: Employer-Backed Block Leases for Hourly Workers
one_liner: A broker that packages 20-100 unit block leases in concession-heavy buildings, backed by an employer's credit guarantee and payroll deduction, to cut rent for hourly workers without raising wages.
customer: Hospital systems, school districts, hotels, casinos and retailers with recruiting and turnover pain, paired with owners of lease-up and high-concession properties who pay the placement fee.
problem: A typical retail worker earns $34,436 against $71,172 needed for a typical $1,779 apartment. Employers lose workers to housing costs, while owners in lease-up hand out 15-37% concessions to anonymous renters and carry 34 days of vacancy.
solution: Negotiate discounted block rents in exchange for guaranteed occupancy. The employer provides a credit guarantee rather than a subsidy, plus optional payroll deduction, and we run eligibility, lease templates, guarantee underwriting and monitoring. The tenant's discount is funded by the owner's savings on concessions, marketing, vacancy and turnover.
why_now: The rental glut and record concessions give owners a reason to trade price for certainty. Employer labor tightness is high, and traditional locators ignore blocks because commissions are small.
revenue_model: Owner-paid placement fee of 3-4% of first-year rent, employer platform fee of $8-15 per enrolled unit per month, and an optional guarantee premium.
non_obvious_insight: The landlord is buying occupancy certainty, not tenants, and avoided concession, vacancy and turnover can approach 10-15% of annual rent, more than a free month per tenant. Employers can create affordability by lending credit instead of paying wages, which also helps them avoid taxable-benefit complications.
first_30_days: Pick Austin or Atlanta. Get three owners with 300+ unit lease-ups to sign a 10%-off block-lease term sheet. Pitch five HR or recruiting heads at hospital and community-college systems. Run one 25-unit pilot and collect the placement fee.

title: Captive Insurer for Hardened Mountain Communities
one_liner: A group cell captive where associations with verified wildfire hardening share first-loss and reinsurance capital.
customer: Condo and townhome associations and mountain-resort communities in California and Colorado with $100K-$1M master premiums, plus their management companies.
problem: Master property premiums have exploded and carriers non-renew whole associations. Reinsurers hold record capital (about $790B, secondary source), yet cannot price unknown community-level risk. Rates fell up to 25% at June 1 2026, but retail carriers pass little through.
solution: A fronted group captive with quota-share reinsurance. Each association's mitigation (IBHS criteria, ember-resistant vents, vegetation plan) is verified and modeled with forward-looking cat models now allowed by California. Members keep the first-loss layer and share the dividends. The first product is captive feasibility plus a verified-hardening scorecard at $15-30K per association, which also improves standard-market placement.
why_now: Howden says reinsurer returns could fall below cost of capital by 2027, so reinsurers want differentiated, verified books now. California's Sustainable Insurance Strategy allows forward-looking models, and Colorado now credits mitigation.
revenue_model: Feasibility fees, then management fees of 8-12% of premium plus ceded profit commission.
non_obvious_insight: The soft reinsurance window is temporary and limited by data quality. Small verified pools can lock multi-year capacity before it hardens.
first_30_days: Meet 3 management companies, score 5 associations, and talk to fronting carriers and captive managers.

title: The 4 A.M. Ride Guild
one_liner: A dispatch network of night-owl local drivers, paid per ride by hospitals and jails, that gets rural patients and released inmates home at hours when Uber and Medicaid rides do not exist.
customer: Critical access hospitals and their foundations, county jails, domestic violence shelters, crisis stabilization units, and Medicaid and Medicare Advantage plans (through value-added benefits). Paid per ride, then by plan contract.
problem: A patient is discharged from a rural ER at 4am. She came by ambulance, her car is 30 miles away, and no taxi, Uber or Lyft exists. Medicaid non-emergency transport needs 24-48 hours notice and does not cover ER discharge. So she sits in the waiting room, a nurse drives her home (against policy), a relative is woken up, or the hospital admits her to observation for 'social reasons', which costs thousands. Jails release people at midnight with no ride, and domestic violence shelters have the same problem in reverse.
solution: A dispatch line (an SMS and phone flow with a human on call, then an app) that promises a driver within 30 minutes anywhere in a county between 10pm and 8am. Supply comes from people who are awake anyway: workers finishing third shift at plants, retired EMTs, volunteer firefighters and off-duty deputies. Riders can be dropped at a hospital, home or shelter, with documented handoff for CMS discharge planning. Add wheelchair-capable vehicles later. Insurance is hired and non-owned auto coverage, and drivers are background checked.
why_now: Rural hospitals are under pressure from Medicaid cuts and closing service lines, so avoiding costly observation stays and unsafe discharges matters more. Rural Health Transformation Program funds can pay for transport and access. Uber Health, Lyft and NEMT brokers are still thin at rural night hours, and the gap is a supply problem software alone cannot fix. Gig-style dispatch and background-check tooling is now cheap enough for a two-person team.
revenue_model: The hospital pays $85-110 per ride and the driver gets $55-65. A monthly minimum of $500-1,500 per facility guarantees driver availability, similar to a retainer. Later add Medicaid MCO and Medicare Advantage value-added benefit contracts. The ride log also supports the hospital's safe-discharge documentation.
non_obvious_insight: Nurses know that the ride is what actually gates a safe discharge at night, and that the hospital quietly pays for it in nurse gas money, observation admissions and ambulance runs. Transport startups assume demand is the hard part. In rural night hours supply is the hard part, and the winning move is recruiting people who are awake at 4am and paying them a guaranteed minimum. Hospital foundations, whose donors like 'getting Grandma home safe', are also a surprisingly easy first funder.
first_30_days: Sign one hospital and one sheriff's office for a pilot with a prepaid $1,000 retainer each. Recruit 15 drivers through third-shift plants, fire department Facebook groups and truck stops. Run dispatch manually via a Twilio group text with the founder on call. Get a hired-and-non-owned auto policy through a commercial broker and run background checks through a screening vendor. Track time to ride and observation stays avoided, and use those to pitch a second and third hospital.

title: Grid-Code Models for AI Data Centers
one_liner: Validated dynamic load models and ride-through test packages so data centers can pass the same grid-code exams that generators pass.
customer: Interconnection teams at hyperscalers, neoclouds and colo developers, and their EPCs. Transmission owners and ISOs need the models validated, and the developer pays.
problem: About 1.5 GW of Northern Virginia data center load tripped offline together during a 2024 fault. AI training loads swing tens of MW in seconds, and xAI buys Megapacks largely to smooth them. Texas SB 6 and NERC large-load work now push for ride-through and dynamic models, but no standard model library or test lab exists for GPU cluster, power-supply and UPS stacks.
solution: Build a parametric EMT and PSS/E model library for common facility architectures (UPS topologies, PSU behavior, 800V DC). Validate it with hardware-in-the-loop tests at a partner lab. Sell per-project model packages, ride-through study reports and compliance-ready certification letters. Charge a subscription to keep models current as hardware changes.
why_now: Multi-GW campuses, NERC's large-load task force and Texas and PJM interconnection rules in 2025-26 are turning load models from optional into a gating item.
revenue_model: $75-300k per project for the model and study, an annual model-maintenance subscription, and test or certification fees paid by UPS and power-shelf OEMs.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone frames data centers as demand. The grid now treats them as a dynamic device, like a giant inverter-based generator. Inverter-generator modeling became a consulting industry after events like the 2016 Blue Cut fire, and large-load modeling will follow. The model library is the moat.
first_30_days: Recruit one or two power-electronics engineers from a utility or ISO. Publish an open primer on GPU-load oscillation. Contact interconnection leads at 10 neoclouds and 5 TO planners. Sell a $15k 'large-load model gap analysis'. Sign a university hardware-in-the-loop lab as a partner.

title: Proof-of-Hours for Medicaid Work Requirements
one_liner: A text-message-first evidence engine that helps gig, seasonal, cash and caregiving enrollees document the 80-hour requirement, paid by managed care plans and safety-net providers for each member retained.
customer: Medicaid managed care plans (revenue is capitation per member), FQHC networks, hospital systems and county health departments carrying uncompensated care. Not the states: federal law bars plans from determining compliance, but outreach and enrollee assistance are allowed.
problem: From 1 Jan 2027, expansion adults 19-64 must show 80 hours a month of work, study or service. CMS projects 2.3 million people lose coverage in FY2027, largely through paperwork failure rather than true non-compliance. Georgia Pathways enrolled only about 16,000 people against roughly 359,000 potentially eligible. Irregular earners (gig, day labor, home care, seasonal, informal) have no clean payroll record, and states mostly rely on payroll data that misses them.
solution: A multilingual SMS, WhatsApp and app 'hour ledger'. It pulls earnings from gig and payment platforms via consented bank or statement links, sends one-tap SMS attestations to employers and clients, and logs volunteer and caregiving hours via QR check-in at partner churches and food banks. It screens for exemptions (medical frailty, caregivers) and outputs the evidence pack in each state's format, with renewal reminders every six months. The member owns the data and the plan sees only consented status.
why_now: Nebraska began enforcement on 1 May 2026. CMS issued its interim final rule on 3 June 2026 defining verification and the 80-hour test, and states did outreach in mid-2026. The national start is 1 Jan 2027 with six-month renewals, and plans are amending contracts now.
revenue_model: A per-member retention bounty ($40-$120 per successful renewal) or PMPM of $2-$6 for high-risk members, paid by plans. FQHC and hospital subscriptions, and later state contracts for outreach.
non_obvious_insight: The fight is not over who is eligible but over who can prove it. Compliant-but-undocumented workers are a large share of those at risk. The party with the strongest incentive to close that gap is not the state but the plan or provider whose revenue disappears with each disenrolled member. Verified hours are a portable asset the member can reuse at every renewal.
first_30_days: Partner with one FQHC network in a live or early-start state such as Nebraska. Hand-run a pilot for 200 enrollees using SMS plus a form, and build evidence-pack templates that match the state portal. Pitch three regional plans on a no-upfront-cost, pay-per-member-retained deal. Get privacy and HIPAA review done before enrolling anyone.

title: Courthouse-Handwriting Graph to Clear Heirs' Property
one_liner: Use AI that can read old handwritten deeds and probate files to map who really owns family land that never went through probate, and sell clean title to the buyers who need it.
customer: Solar, wind, pipeline and broadband developers, land trusts and conservation buyers, timber and ag buyers, and title insurers, with legal-aid partners protecting heirs.
problem: When a landowner dies without probate, title fragments among dozens of heirs. Developers can't lease or buy without consent, and heirs can lose land through partition sales. The records are handwritten across probate, deed and marriage files, so clearing one parcel takes lawyers weeks or months.
solution: LLM handwriting recognition over courthouse records builds a family-of-record graph per parcel, ranks probable heirs, finds them, and manages consent, lease or purchase packages through e-signature. Partner attorneys file quiet-title or partition actions for hard cases. Developers get a 'title-readiness score' per parcel. The design bakes in fair terms and legal aid for heirs.
why_now: Multimodal models now read historical cursive at near-human accuracy, and county records are increasingly scanned. The Uniform Partition of Heirs Property Act has been adopted in a couple dozen states, which pushes toward consensual deals. The land rush for solar and data-center sites needs clean title fast.
revenue_model: $2K-$10K per cleared parcel paid by the developer or a percentage of lease value, plus data licensing to title insurers.
non_obvious_insight: The transfer that never went through probate, family land passed informally for generations, is a hidden inventory of blocked assets. Now a buyer with money (energy and data infrastructure) will pay to clear it.
first_30_days: Pick one county in a solar-active area with high heirs' property prevalence. Get a developer's list of blocked parcels. Process 10 parcels and partner with a heirs' property legal clinic to review the process and heir outreach.

title: Pay-Per-Win Appeals Desk for Nursing Homes
one_liner: A 24/7 appeal desk that turns every Medicare Advantage post-acute denial and coverage-termination notice into a filed appeal, paid only when the plan reverses.
customer: Independent and regional skilled nursing operators (3-30 facilities), plus home health agencies and inpatient rehab units that live on Medicare Advantage authorizations and have no appeals staff.
problem: A federal OIG review reported by Healthcare Dive found MA plans denied about 12% of SNF requests, about 67% of LTACH and over 50% of inpatient-rehab requests. SNFs appealed fewer than 20% of denials, yet 95% of those appeals were overturned (UnitedHealth 99.7%). Across all MA, KFF found 53M prior-auth decisions in 2024, 7.7% denied, only 11.5% of denials appealed, and more than 8 in 10 appeals won. Denied days are unpaid receivables that never get worked, because business-office staff have no time.
solution: Read-only integration with the SNF's EHR (for example PointClickCare) plus a shared inbox for plan letters. On each denial or non-coverage notice, the system builds the clinical packet (therapy minutes, nursing notes, MDS data) mapped to Traditional Medicare coverage criteria, which MA plans must follow under the 2024 CMS rule. It drafts the reconsideration or fast-track appeal, tracks the deadlines (including the noon-the-day-before deadline for fast-track requests), and escalates to independent review. A contract RN reviews and signs. Plan-specific playbooks learn what each plan responds to.
why_now: The OIG reports came out in June 2026 and were widely covered. CMS-0057-F public reporting now shows plan-level denial and overturn data (first-of-its-kind data in August 2026: 1 in 8 standard requests denied, about two-thirds of MA appeals won). Providers can now show a board or CFO the expected value of appeals. LLM drafting makes per-appeal cost low enough to work small denials.
revenue_model: Contingency of 15-25% of recovered per-diem revenue, only on overturned denials. Optional SaaS tier for chains that want the workflow in-house.
non_obvious_insight: A 95% overturn rate with fewer than 20% of denials appealed means the constraint is clerk hours, not merits. The unworked denial pile is the largest uncollected receivable in post-acute care, and success-only pricing removes the operator's risk. Evidence: OIG results via Healthcare Dive (https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/medicare-advantage-prior-authorization-denials-hhs-oig-post-acute-care/822724/), KFF's 53M-determination analysis (https://www.kff.org/medicare/issue-brief/medicare-advantage-insurers-made-nearly-53-million-prior-authorization-determinations-in-2024/), and 2026 plan-level metrics (https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/prior-authorization-denials-vary-widely-among-insurers/827891/). Competition is real in general appeals automation, so the wedge is SNF-specific workflow plus a contingency contract, not a generic appeals tool.
first_30_days: Recruit 3 small SNF chains through state nursing-home associations. Backfill their last 6-12 months of MA denials to show a retroactive expected win rate. Sign BAAs and start filing live appeals by week 3 on a no-win-no-fee basis. Hire one part-time contract RN reviewer. Start with the two or three plans with the highest SNF denial rates and build their playbooks first.

title: Scam-Baiting AI Fleet Selling Mule Intel
one_liner: Thousands of realistic AI victims answer scammers' calls and chats around the clock, extract the accounts and wallets they are told to pay, and hand them to the holding institutions before real victims do.
customer: Banks, neobanks, BaaS sponsor banks, stablecoin issuers, exchanges and payment apps. Telcos are a secondary buyer.
problem: Scam cash-out depends on mule accounts and wallets, but institutions learn about them only after victims pay. Scam revenue reached about $17B in 2025, and AI-enabled operations earn far more per operation, while defense stays manual and reactive.
solution: Persona-driven voice and messaging agents on real-time speech-to-speech models answer phone numbers seeded onto scam lead lists and respond to smishing and wrong-number openers. They keep scammers engaged (burning their labor), record payment instructions, and extract payee accounts, wallets and gift-card destinations. Evidence-graded indicators go via API to the institution that holds the account so it can freeze and close before a real victim pays.
why_now: Real-time speech models made convincing multi-turn calls cheap in 2025-26. Stablecoin issuers and cross-industry units now freeze funds quickly, and the US-UK scam-center coordination raises appetite for actionable intelligence.
revenue_model: $200-1,000 per confirmed account or wallet plus $5-20K per month subscriptions, and data licensing to fraud vendors.
non_obvious_insight: Scammers' scarce resource is human operator time, so AI victims raise their cost per victim while producing intelligence with zero victim cost. Institutions pay far more for pre-loss intelligence than for post-loss forensics.
first_30_days: Build 20 personas across phone and WhatsApp. Run them against inbound spam numbers and produce about 100 verified indicators. Sell 2 neobanks and 1 exchange a $10K paid pilot, with counsel reviewing recording-consent rules first.

title: Prize-Money Payout and Tax Rail for Tournaments
one_liner: Payout operations for tournament organizers and esports orgs: one-time player KYC and tax onboarding, treaty-aware withholding, sanctions screening, and multi-currency payment.
customer: Mid-tier tournament organizers (regional leagues, publisher-sanctioned circuits, fighting-game majors) and esports orgs receiving club-program stipends.
problem: Prize money exploded, with $75M at the 2026 Esports World Cup (moved to Paris) and a $20M club partner program across 40 orgs. Payments go to players in dozens of countries, including minors, with tax forms, withholding and sanctions checks, and organizers run it on spreadsheets and wire transfers.
solution: A payout platform with a portable 'player payout profile' (KYC and tax forms collected once), automated withholding by treaty, sanctions screening, escrowed prize pools released on verified results, and payment on local rails. Add visa and travel letter templates and year-end tax reporting.
why_now: Sovereign money inflated prize pools, and the Saudi-Olympic Esports Games partnership ending (2025-10-30) pushes more independent circuits. The compliance burden has grown with the money.
revenue_model: 1-2% of payout volume plus $3-8 per payee, and $500-3,000 per month SaaS for orgs.
non_obvious_insight: Prize pools stopped being a marketing line item and became a payments-and-tax operations problem. The onboarding data is portable across events, so each player carried through one event lowers the cost for the next organizer.
first_30_days: Interview 15 tournament organizers via start.gg and fighting-game communities. Run payouts manually for two events at 1.5% to learn the edge cases, and build the KYC and tax-form intake.

title: Sovereign Data Vaults in Orbit
one_liner: Encrypted national-records backups stored in orbit, out of reach of seizure, cyber-wipe or flood.
customer: Governments of small, exposed or at-risk states (Baltics, Pacific island nations, Ukraine, Taiwan-type buyers), central banks and national archives.
problem: Countries already run 'data embassies' in friendly data centers, but those still sit on someone's soil. A wipe, seizure, war or sea-level loss can strand civil registries, land titles and treasury records.
solution: Start with a hosted-payload vault on a partner satellite: an append-only, radiation-tolerant encrypted store holding registries and legal records, with keys held by the customer under multi-party control and a dead-man retrieval process. Grow into dedicated vault satellites.
why_now: Rideshare pricing makes small payloads cheap. 2025 demonstrations of storage and compute in orbit (Lonestar's data payloads, Starcloud's reported H100 launch) showed the concept works. Geopolitical risk to state data has risen.
revenue_model: Feasibility studies $50-150k. Multi-year vault contracts of $1-5M per year. Per-TB-year storage fees after launch.
non_obvious_insight: Governments already pay for offshore backups. The extraterritorial jurisdiction of orbit can be sold as a legal and physical guarantee, not as a gadget.
first_30_days: Approach digital-government offices in Estonia, Tuvalu, Ukraine and Taiwan-type buyers with a paid feasibility study. Line up a hosted-payload slot with an existing operator. Design the key-custody model with a legal adviser on treaty and jurisdiction questions.

title: Zero-Retention Edge Enforcement for City Cameras
one_liner: Privacy-proof add-on analytics for existing plate readers and CCTV that keep only violation events and cryptographically delete everything else.
customer: Mid-size cities and towns in states that authorize automated enforcement (noise, illegal dumping, stop-arm, blocked bus lanes), starting with Connecticut, plus police departments under pressure over Flock-style data retention.
problem: Connecticut towns are bolting audio detectors onto existing plate readers for noise enforcement, while Ohio bills and public backlash attack camera surveillance. Cities want the revenue but fear becoming the next headline about bulk data retention.
solution: Edge box or firmware add-on that runs detection on-device and stores only the evidence clip for a confirmed violation. Everything else is deleted with signed deletion logs that auditors can verify. Sold as a rev-share enforcement program with a city-adoptable privacy ordinance template.
why_now: Connecticut's 2024 noise-camera law is live in West Haven, Wethersfield and East Hartford. Ohio bills show the Flock backlash is turning legislative. Cheap edge inference makes on-device analytics viable.
revenue_model: Per-citation or per-camera-month fee (for example 20-30% of net citation revenue, or $150-300 per camera per month), plus a one-time install fee.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders read the backlash as the end of sensor stacking. It is actually a moat for whoever makes data architecturally un-repurposable. Privacy becomes the procurement feature that survives a city council vote.
first_30_days: Pitch 5 Connecticut towns already running noise pilots to add a pilot with a retention-proof log. Build the demo on an off-the-shelf edge board with an existing LPR feed. Draft the ordinance template with a municipal attorney.

title: Bonded US-Only Remote Operators for Robots
one_liner: A staffing company for physical AI: background-checked, bonded, US-resident remote operators working from secure facilities on SLA-backed shifts to assist robotaxis, delivery robots and teleoperated humanoids.
customer: AV fleets, sidewalk and delivery robot operators, humanoid and mobile-manipulation startups (Series A to C) and the enterprise or health customers who demand US-based, vetted humans. The buyer is the head of operations or safety.
problem: Autonomy plateaus at 99%, and the last 1% is human labor. Waymo disclosed at a February 2026 Senate hearing that some remote assistance staff are in the Philippines, drawing political heat (Sen. Markey called it a safety issue). 1X's Neo puts a remote operator with a VR headset inside customers' homes, which is the central privacy objection. Robot startups have no staffing operation for 24/7 shift coverage, vetting, training, security controls and quality scoring.
solution: Secure operator centers (not homes) staffed with vetted US-resident operators drawn from gamers, drone pilots, veterans and military spouses. Certification per partner interface, quality scoring, audit trails and a 'named operator and session log' feature so a homeowner or hospital can see who touched what. Start with teleoperation for data collection and pilot demos, then move into live remote assistance and compliance packs.
why_now: Consumer humanoids and expanding robotaxi fleets (Waymo alone is at about 500k paid rides a week across 14 cities) make operator-hours a rapidly scaling cost. The Senate scrutiny of offshore remote assistance and the Neo privacy debate mean a 'US-only, vetted, auditable' premium is about to be demanded by regulators and enterprise buyers.
revenue_model: Billed operator-hours at $40-70/hour against a loaded cost of $25-30/hour. Premiums for compliance, security clearance and named-operator features. Setup fees for integration and certification.
non_obvious_insight: Every 10,000 robots create thousands of operator jobs, and the political fight will be about where those people sit, just as with call centers. Whoever builds the trusted, audited labor pool early owns a compliance premium that AI labs cannot easily build in-house.
first_30_days: Rent a 10-seat secured room in a mid-cost city. Buy Quest headsets and a leader-follower arm set. Recruit 15 operators from gaming and RC-drone communities and pass them through background checks. Offer 100 pilot-hours at cost-plus to 10 humanoid and delivery-robot startups who need demo and data collection help.

title: Kitchen Circuit Retrofit for India's Induction Switch
one_liner: Induction demand is real but low-income wiring cannot handle it, so sell the safe electrical retrofit and finance it.
customer: Lower-income urban households and resident welfare associations, reached through local electricians and hardware shops; discoms and state schemes can co-fund.
problem: After the LPG shortage, induction cooktop demand jumped 20-25x, the government is handing out 500k stoves, and the shift could add up to 27 GW. The Hindu reports low-income uptake is sluggish because of old wiring, overloaded meters and no financing.
solution: A pre-certified plug-and-play kit: dedicated 16A circuit, MCB/RCCB, heavy-duty socket and load-limiting smart plug, installed in two hours and paid in 12 EMIs. The wedge is 500 homes in one city through about 30 electricians.
why_now: The Hormuz energy shock created panic demand in March 2026, and the grid and household wiring are the binding constraint.
revenue_model: Rs 2,500-4,000 per kit and install at about 30% margin, plus an EMI spread and programme fees from discoms.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone counts stoves sold. The bottleneck is the last 15 metres of copper, and the first fire wave will turn certified retrofits into a regulated must-buy.
first_30_days: Design the kit with a licensed electrical engineer and pre-sell it through 20 electricians and one housing association.

title: Patent-Grade Variant Maps for Biologics
one_liner: Pooled-screening service that generates the sequence-function data biologics patents now need after Amgen v. Sanofi, plus a mirror-image design-around report for companies facing sequence claims.
customer: IP counsel and patent boutiques at antibody and protein biotechs, biosimilar and biobetter developers, and mid-size biotechs working in crowded target classes.
problem: Trend chain: Amgen v. Sanofi (2023) killed functional genus antibody claims unless the specification enables the full scope. Patents therefore shrink toward sequence-specific claims backed by data. Counsel typically has data on 20-50 variants. Meanwhile cheap DNA and AI design make thousands of function-preserving variants easy to produce, so both breadth-by-data (offense) and design-around (defense) become experimental problems that no one packages.
solution: Offense: pooled display or mammalian screening of 10^4-10^6 designed variants with NGS readout, delivered as patent-ready sequence-function tables and generalizations (which CDR positions tolerate what) to support broader claims. Defense: search patent sequence claims, compute identity against claim thresholds, design function-preserving escapes and validate the top candidates in a pool. Sold through IP counsel, not legal advice.
why_now: DNA is no longer the cost: Weizmann built 2.5 billion antibody fragments on phage for EUR 38,000 of DNA. Zero-shot design tools generate variants at scale. Post-Amgen enablement pressure has had three years to bite, and law-firm commentary is now explicitly tackling AI and enablement.
revenue_model: $40-150k per patent family for offense work, $8-25k per FTO or design-around candidate, and subscriptions for boutiques.
non_obvious_insight: With cheap DNA and pooled assays, 'enablement by data' becomes a commodity for whoever runs the experiment. Patent breadth turns into a function of wet-lab throughput rather than lawyer cleverness. The same machine that broadens your claims also narrows a competitor's, so buyers exist on both sides of every thicket.
first_30_days: Sign 3 IP boutiques as design partners. Build a claim-matching tool on public USPTO and EPO sequence listings. Offer 10 free FTO scans. Contract a pooled-display partner. Price one paid offense pilot with a biotech preparing a continuation filing.

title: Corridor-Pivot Recruiting for Displaced Gulf Migrants
one_liner: When Gulf jobs disappear, retrain returnees and place them in Japan, Taiwan and Germany with the employer paying the fee.
customer: Employers in care, construction and manufacturing in East Asia and Europe that pay placement fees; the workers pay nothing.
problem: About $50bn of Gulf remittances is at risk. Returnees in Kerala, Nepal, Bangladesh and the Philippines carry recruitment debts and Gulf-specific credentials, and predatory agents will push them into worse corridors.
solution: A skills-credential wallet, language bootcamp and employer-paid placement pipeline, operated through a licensed recruitment partner. The wedge is care workers and welders from Kerala and Nepal for one Japanese or German employer.
why_now: The 2026 Iran-war energy shock displaced workers, and ageing economies are widening visa routes for care and trades.
revenue_model: $1.5-3k employer placement fee per worker, plus employer-paid training subscriptions.
non_obvious_insight: Displaced migrants are a supply shock nobody is organising. Employer-pays recruitment is both ethical and the direction of ILO fair-recruitment rules.
first_30_days: Sign one Kerala training institute and one overseas care-home operator, and run 30 candidates through a pilot.

title: Idle-Still Co-Packing for Zero-Proof Brands
one_liner: Turn distilleries' idle stills and bottling lines into contract capacity for dealcoholized and botanical spirit brands.
customer: Craft and mid-size distilleries with underused capacity, and zero-proof beverage brands that need production.
problem: US spirits sales fell 15.4% and Diageo's US tequila fell 23% as GLP-1 use spreads, leaving distilleries with fixed costs and empty lines.
solution: A capacity broker and operations layer that matches idle distilleries to zero-proof and functional-tonic brands, handles TTB and formulation paperwork, and standardizes QA and scheduling.
why_now: GLP-1 adoption is now visibly cutting alcohol volumes, and the non-alcoholic segment is growing but short of contract capacity with spirit-grade distillation.
revenue_model: 10-15% take on co-pack contracts plus fees for compliance and formulation services.
non_obvious_insight: The first casualties of GLP-1 in beverages are asset-heavy distillers, whose stills are worth more as co-packers to the segment that is replacing them. Grain and agave growers downstream are the next to feel it.
first_30_days: Interview 20 distilleries about idle capacity, line up 5 zero-proof brands with pending production needs, and run one paid pilot batch with a partner distillery.

title: Collective Anti-Piracy Desk for 3D-Print Miniature Creators
one_liner: A creator-owned enforcement collective that fingerprints STL/3D-print models, hunts leaks across Telegram, Discord and marketplaces, and uses EU Digital Services Act notice, trusted-flagger and appeal rights to make takedowns stick.
customer: Independent sculptors and small studios selling printable miniatures, terrain and tabletop models via Patreon, Kickstarter, MyMiniFactory, Cults3D and their own stores (tens of thousands worldwide, top creators earning six figures). Also indie designers of other collectible models (keyboard cases, cosplay props) and the hosting platforms that want a clean enforcement feed.
problem: Files leak within days of release, spread through Discord and Telegram, get resold on Etsy/eBay/Temu-style marketplaces and printed into physical minis. A solo creator faces hundreds of infringements a month, and one-by-one DMCA notices cost hours, are ignored or are countered by repeat offenders. Brand-protection vendors price for brands, not solo sculptors. The EU Digital Services Act gave structured levers (Art. 16 notice-and-action, Art. 17 statements of reasons, Art. 21 out-of-court dispute bodies, Art. 22 trusted-flagger priority) and put very large marketplaces such as Temu and AliExpress under Commission supervision, but nobody has packaged these levers for small creators.
solution: (1) Geometry-based mesh fingerprinting, robust to re-meshing, scaling, splitting and hollowing, plus image similarity for renders and prints, with crawlers for leak channels, marketplaces and cloud-drive links. (2) A case engine that files DMCA and DSA notices in correct legal form, tracks counter-notices and statements of reasons, and escalates repeat infringers to the platform's regulator complaint channels. (3) An EU-established entity built to apply for DSA trusted-flagger status; Art. 22 explicitly favors bodies that represent collective interests and are independent of platforms. (4) A 'legit copy' program that offers print farms and Etsy resellers a licensed route, so leaks become royalty income.
why_now: The printable-model economy on Patreon and 3D-printer adoption are at scale. The DSA has been fully applicable since Feb 2024 and the Commission's 2025 actions against Temu/AliExpress make regulator escalation credible (verify status). AI re-meshing and generative 3D tools make exact-hash detection obsolete. Pressure from IP owners like Games Workshop pushes hobbyists toward original designs, so creator-owned IP is growing.
revenue_model: Subscriptions of $29-149/month by catalog size. 10-20% share of licensed royalties recovered from converted resellers. Enterprise feed for hosting platforms that want a vetted trusted-flagger channel.
non_obvious_insight: Piracy at this scale is a coordination problem. Thirty thousand creators each losing $5-50k cannot afford lawyers, but as a collective with formal DSA status they generate volume and quality that platforms must prioritise. The realistic prize is converting pirates into licensees (print farms reselling legally), not just takedown counts.
first_30_days: Sign 10 mid-tier Patreon sculptors for a free 30-day leak report. Build the fingerprint and crawler MVP with open-source mesh-hashing plus CLIP embeddings. Send DMCA/DSA notices through a part-time attorney and measure takedown rates. Convert reports to $49/month subscriptions. Register the EU entity and start the trusted-flagger application with counsel.

title: FEOC and Cyber Passport for Batteries
one_liner: A serial-number-level ledger of material-assistance content and firmware and comms attestations for storage projects, built for tax-credit buyers and insurers.
customer: C&I and utility-scale storage developers and integrators, tax-credit transfer buyers (banks and insurers), and lenders.
problem: FEOC rules require 55% non-FEOC content for storage starting construction in 2026, rising to 75% by 2030. About 80% of US cells are Chinese and non-compliant projects run about 43% pricier. IRS cost tables are not due until 2027, so nobody can prove compliance. Buyers of tax credits and insurers need evidence, and concern about undocumented radios in imported inverters adds a cyber layer.
solution: A workflow and ledger that captures the bill of materials at cell and module level with supplier attestations and cost tables, then computes the material-assistance ratio conservatively. Each project gets an audit-ready evidence packet. Optional teardown, RF and firmware attestation runs through a partner lab. The 'passport' is what transfer buyers and insurers accept.
why_now: FEOC applies to 2026 construction starts, the tax-credit transfer market is doing diligence at scale, and tariffs are rising.
revenue_model: $15-50k per project, $2-5k a month SaaS per developer, verification fees from transfer buyers, and cost-plus lab attestation.
non_obvious_insight: The burden is evidence, not sourcing. With IRS guidance missing, the first firm whose conservative methodology gets accepted becomes the de facto standard, and insurers will only underwrite recapture cover against that record.
first_30_days: Publish a free MACR calculator with conservative assumptions. Interview 10 developers and three tax-credit transfer buyers. Sell three paid compliance-file builds at ~$15k for 2026-start projects. Pre-agree terms with an attestation lab.

title: Unlisted: The Agent-Proof Offline Guide
one_liner: A numbered, mailed-only paper guide plus a human phone line for restaurants, bars, and shops that deliberately cannot be found or booked by AI agents.
customer: Affluent urbanites (30-60) paying $250-400/year, capped at about 2,000 members per city. Corporate concierge and client-gifting accounts pay $5-20k/year. Venues pay nothing, which keeps the guide's independence.
problem: ChatGPT began booking tables through OpenTable, Resy, and Yelp on 10 August 2026, and Gemini, Alexa+, and Perplexity have similar integrations. Everyone's agent now picks the same top-ranked places, bots snipe scarce tables, and Resy prohibits unsanctioned agents. 'I found this place' no longer signals taste, and small venues that want regulars rather than scale have no way to opt out of the flood.
solution: A quarterly printed booklet of 40-60 venues per city, compiled by scouts who visit anonymously. It is posted to members and never published as a PDF. Each entry has a phone number for the Unlisted line, a human-staffed concierge that books by voice, or a door code word, and never an online booking link. Fictional 'canary' details in entries let the guide trace leaks. Members agree to a no-posting norm and are expelled for breaking it. Venues get vetted, lower-no-show clientele.
why_now: Agentic booking went mainstream in August 2026 and venues are reacting with bot bans. Platform algorithms now homogenize discovery. Freelance food and travel writers are being laid off, so scout supply is cheap and high quality.
revenue_model: $250-400/year membership. Corporate concierge accounts. Paid members-only events in venues (ticketed, with the venue's cut waived). Possible city-by-city licensing to local scouts later.
non_obvious_insight: When discovery is automated, unindexability becomes the scarce good. The guide earns trust by refusing to be online, and its scarcity is enforced by physical media and an honor code. Its value is negative space that AI agents structurally cannot see.
first_30_days: Pick one city and hire 3-4 laid-off food writers as scouts. Post a teaser page with no venue names and pre-sell 300 founding memberships at $200. Print 500 numbered copies. Run the phone line on a shared business number with two part-timers. Test the model by having a scout call in a booking.

title: Independent Auditor of Real Agent-Commerce Volume
one_liner: A neutral measurement firm that separates real agent payments from wash trading and testing, then sells diligence to investors and behavioral AML monitoring to the trust banks that carry the flows.
customer: Investors and acquirers diligencing agent-payment startups, protocol foundations and ecosystem funds that allocate grants on volume, OCC-chartered trust banks, stablecoin issuers and MSBs onboarding agent-wallet fintechs, and card networks and acquirers.
problem: Bloomberg found that about $24M of on-chain agent commerce shrinks to about $1.6M once self-trading wallets are removed, and Base logged about 97M protocol transactions with no one able to say how many were live. Meanwhile Tempo raised $500M and every network is announcing agent rails. KYC at onboarding does not fit wallets that act autonomously, and continuous behavioral KYC is the flagged gap.
solution: Cluster wallets, detect self-dealing, and classify each flow as test, wash or real economic activity (unique counterparties, fiat off-ramps, merchant tie-outs) across x402, MPP and AP2 settlement. Publish a free index, sell diligence reports, and offer an agent-tuned monitoring API that scores velocity, counterparty concentration and sanctions-adjacent exposure for BSA/AML programs.
why_now: x402 moved to the Linux Foundation in April 2026 and MPP is live. The Fed proposed GENIUS Act issuer rules on 2026-09-24, and OCC trust charters are being handed out (Circle on 2026-07-10, Coinbase in April, Bridge conditionally). A Senate report alleging about $2B of Iran-linked Tether flows raises the cost of weak compliance.
revenue_model: Diligence engagements at $15-60k each, monitoring subscriptions at $5-30k per month per bank or issuer, and data licensing to funds and networks.
non_obvious_insight: In a hype market the scarce good is credible measurement, and a firm with no token or protocol stake is the only party everyone can trust. The clustering work that debunks the volume numbers is the same compliance product regulated banks will have to buy, and it needs both on-chain forensics and agent-protocol fluency.
first_30_days: Two on-chain analysts build the wash filter on public data (Dune or Flipside), publish 'Real vs Reported Agent Commerce' with an open methodology, and pitch it to 15 funds and 3 foundations. Charge for the first bespoke diligence report within the month, and let the free index drive inbound.

title: Pooled Guaranteed Throughput for Agent Builders
one_liner: Mid-market agent builders cannot meet reserved-capacity minimums, so we pool dozens of them into one commitment and sell guaranteed tokens-per-minute with failover.
customer: Agent-heavy SaaS companies and enterprise platform teams with $20k-$300k/month in model spend that hit rate limits and latency spikes at burst but cannot fill provisioned-throughput commitments.
problem: One agent task fans out into dozens of model and tool calls, multiplying request volume 10-50x. Provider tokens-per-minute ceilings and noisy neighbors cause 429s and latency spikes exactly when workflows burst. Reserved throughput exists but is sized for peak and billed monthly, so a mid-market buyer pays for capacity idle most of the day.
solution: A CSP-style aggregator and gateway that buys committed capacity across 2-3 providers, statistically multiplexes customers whose peaks do not coincide, and sells guaranteed-TPM slices with consolidated billing, per-tenant quotas and automatic cross-provider failover. Begin as a failover gateway, then graduate to pooled commitments once demand data proves the multiplexing gain.
why_now: Token prices fell about 67% in a year while agentic usage per task rose 5-30x, so capacity, not unit price, binds at peak. The gateway and sandbox layers are commoditizing (identical sandbox pricing), leaving supply-side pooling as a differentiator.
revenue_model: 10-20% spread on committed spend plus a platform fee for guaranteed-capacity tiers.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone frames the problem as price, but for agents the binding constraint is burst capacity when a workflow fans out. Burstiness is diversifiable, like classic insurance pooling, and small buyers cannot pool on their own.
first_30_days: Launch a failover gateway with consolidated billing across Bedrock, Vertex and Azure (no commitment). Sign 10 design partners and collect hourly usage data, model the multiplexing gain, and negotiate the first pooled commitment with letters of intent in hand.

title: Hospital-Guaranteed Loans for Excluded Health Programs
one_liner: Employer-cosigned, service-obligation tuition loans for nursing, OT, PT and counseling students that the new federal caps abandoned.
customer: Hospital systems, rural health networks, behavioral-health agencies and skilled-nursing chains (they guarantee or buy down); their incoming students and employees; a CDFI or specialty-finance fund as capital partner.
problem: Since July 1, 2026 Grad PLUS is gone, grad loans are capped at $20.5k per year and $100k total, and nursing, OT, PT, counseling, psychology and social work were excluded from the higher 'professional' cap. Private lenders are tightening, and predatory loans run up to 16% APR. These fields face the most AI-resistant shortages, including nurse educators, NPs and therapists.
solution: A loan product with employer guarantee or interest buy-down, a 2-3 year service commitment, and retention-linked forgiveness paid by the employer as tenure accrues. Underwrite on licensure pass rates and a signed job offer rather than FICO. The employer gets a cheaper pipeline and retention tool than agency staffing or sign-on bonuses.
why_now: The cap regime took effect in July 2026. A healthcare-association lawsuit is pending, with a December 2026 suspension deadline, so uncertainty is high. Incumbent lenders are retreating. Hospitals are under labor-cost pressure.
revenue_model: 2-3% origination fee, servicing spread, and a per-participant employer program fee. Use a bank-partner or licensed-lender model at first so you don't need your own lending licenses.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders read the cap as proof these programs are too risky to finance. In fact, licensure-gated wages and very high employment make them among the best credits in higher ed. The natural underwriter is not a bank but the employer who would otherwise pay a large premium for temporary staff.
first_30_days: Pick one state and 2 hospital systems that already run tuition assistance. Pitch a $2M pilot warehouse line from a CDFI or hospital foundation for about 20 students starting January 2027. Engage a licensed bank or lender partner and counsel on structure.

title: CRA Technical-File Compiler Built Into CI
one_liner: A GitHub/GitLab app that assembles the Cyber Resilience Act technical documentation, Annex I evidence and draft declaration of conformity from every release, so compliance is a build artifact rather than a consulting project.
customer: Product-security leads and CTOs at connected-device makers with 20-300 engineers (smart home, industrial IoT, e-bikes, wearables, network gear, EV chargers) selling into the EU. Not the GRC team.
problem: CRA reporting duties began 11 Sep 2026, full application is 11 Dec 2027, and fines reach EUR 15M or 2.5% of turnover. Manufacturers must keep versioned technical documentation (risk assessment, design, vulnerability handling, test evidence, SBOM), for roughly ten years or the support period. GRC platforms produce policy evidence, SBOM tools produce component lists, and consultants charge tens of thousands per product line for a file that goes stale on the next release.
solution: The app reads the repo, CI logs, SBOM (SPDX/CycloneDX), threat-model files and test results, then maps them to the Annex I essential requirements and vulnerability-handling duties. It posts gaps as pull-request comments ('no secure-update mechanism documented'). Each release yields a signed, timestamped technical-file bundle (PDF plus machine-readable), a declaration-of-conformity draft, a support-period statement and a diff from the previous release.
why_now: Reporting is already live and full application is 15 months away, so products in design today are locking in the choices that determine compliance cost. Harmonised standards are still arriving, so teams need structured evidence now rather than a finished standard to tick off.
revenue_model: SaaS at $1,500-6,000/month per product line, EUR 5-15k onboarding, and referral revenue from test labs and notified bodies.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders assume Vanta/Drata-style GRC platforms will absorb the CRA. But the CRA is product regulation: the evidence lives in Git, CI and design docs and must be regenerated each release. That is a developer-tool, bottom-up sale to engineers, not a compliance-officer sale.
first_30_days: Interview 15 device makers via CRA meetups and open-source foundations working on CRA. Build a CLI that ingests a CycloneDX SBOM plus a small cra.yaml and emits a skeleton technical file. Run three paid pilots (EUR 3-5k) that produce each firm's first file, and publish the Annex I checklist as open source to draw inbound.

title: Signed Live Recordings from Every Small Venue
one_liner: A cheap box that records a small venue's mixing-desk multitrack, signs it with time and place, and delivers the artist a 'recorded live tonight' release within hours.
customer: Touring indie artists (per-show packages) and small venues of 25-500 capacity (hosts and revenue partners), later promoters and ticketing.
problem: The one thing AI cannot fabricate is a specific night in a specific room. Yet tens of thousands of small shows happen nightly with no recording, while generative music floods the shelf. Bandcamp's AI ban made it a natural home for human-made music, and artists have few new products to sell there.
solution: Software on a mini-PC or a $300-500 box connects to common digital consoles (Behringer X32/Midas-class, Allen & Heath) over USB or network to capture multitrack audio. It timestamps with network time and location, signs a C2PA audio manifest, auto-mixes with ML, and delivers a release and shareable page within hours. Venues get a share of sales, and a public ledger builds over time.
why_now: C2PA supports audio, generative music has made 'real and live' a scarcity signal, cheap mini-PCs and ML auto-mixing exist, and Bandcamp is positioned as a human-only marketplace.
revenue_model: $99-199 per show for the artist, or $79/month per venue plus 20% of release sales, with hardware leased at about $399.
non_obvious_insight: Provenance of place and time is unforgeable in a way that process proof is not. A live album also turns authenticity into a revenue-producing product instead of a cost.
first_30_days: Wire up 5 friendly venues in one city with X32 consoles. Hand-mix the first shows. Sell 'live release in 24 hours' to 20 touring bands at $99 through booking agents, and track Bandcamp sales.
